title: Review: IUPAC nomenclature; Structural isomerism; Alkanes, fuels and cracking
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR04#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR03#N.4, OR04#N.4, OR06#N.17, OR03#N.7, OR04#N.7, OR06#N.14, OR03#N.10, OR04#N.9, OR06#N.11, OR03#N.11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Functional group isomers
items.clue: One molecular formula but different families, e.g. propanal and propanone.

items.label: Incomplete combustion
items.clue: Burning of an alkane in limited oxygen, giving CO and/or C as well as H₂O.

items.label: Tertiary alcohol
items.clue: The carbon carrying the –OH is bonded to three other carbons, as in (CH₃)₃COH.

items.label: Chain isomers
items.clue: One molecular formula but different carbon skeletons, e.g. hexane and 2-methylpentane.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂Cl?
questions.explanation: Longest chain four carbons. Numbering from the CH₂Cl end gives {1, 2}, lower than {3, 4}. Prefixes alphabetical.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are position isomers?
questions.explanation: Both are C₅H₁₂O alcohols on the same unbranched chain; only the –OH position differs (pentan-1-ol, pentan-3-ol).

questions.stem: A gas heater burns methane in a small room. The window is shut and the air vent is blocked. Why is this dangerous?

options.text: Methane burns completely, and the carbon dioxide that forms is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so CO forms, which cuts the oxygen that blood can carry.
Oxygen runs short, so unburned methane builds up, and methane is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so the hydrogen in methane escapes as poisonous hydrogen gas.

questions.explanation: Limited oxygen gives incomplete combustion. CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than O₂ does. It has no colour or smell.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO?
questions.explanation: Four-carbon chain including the –CHO carbon, which is C1. The methyl is on C2.

questions.stem: Which compound is a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanation: The carbon carrying –OH is bonded to three carbons (two CH₃, one CH₂CH₃): 2-methylbutan-2-ol is tertiary.

questions.stem: Which pollutant in car exhaust forms from the air rather than from the fuel?
questions.explanation: Air is mostly N₂ and O₂. At the high temperature inside an engine they combine: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO. The fuel contains no nitrogen.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: Six-carbon chain. From the left, the C=O is on C3 (from the right, C4) and the methyl on C5.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers, hexane included, have the molecular formula C₆H₁₄?
questions.explanation: Hexane; 2-methylpentane; 3-methylpentane; 2,2-dimethylbutane; 2,3-dimethylbutane. Every other drawing is one of these.

questions.stem: Methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen. Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon is deposited as soot, while the hydrogen still forms water. 1 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.
pent: five-carbon chain. -2-one: C=O on C2. 3-methyl: a CH₃ branch on C3.
